intro.title: useImperativeHandle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with a custom input component that allows a parent component to programmatically trigger a focus action on it. You will learn the core concept of `useImperativeHandle`, a React Hook that lets you customize the instance value that is exposed when a parent component uses `ref` on a child. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and the `forwardRef` API to pass refs through components. This lesson will show you how to control child component behaviors from a parent, a useful pattern for imperative actions like focusing, scrolling, or media playback.
intro.usecase: In real applications, useImperativeHandle is commonly used when parent components need to directly control child component behavior that isn't naturally exposed through props. For example, in complex form libraries, parent form components often need to programmatically trigger validation or reset functions on specific input fields. This pattern appears in dashboard components where a main panel needs to scroll a nested chart into view, or in modal systems where a parent needs to manually focus the first input when a modal opens. It's particularly useful for creating reusable component libraries where you want to expose specific imperative methods while keeping the component's internal implementation encapsulated.
